question: does the seed spread of adversarial debiasing on CelebA belong to the method or to the configuration selected at seed 0?
budget: full training budget, identical to the reported pass
statistic: standard deviation over the five seeds of test worst-group accuracy

rule.method: both configurations with lambda >= 0.1 other than the frozen one (t3, t6) exceed the threshold
rule.configuration: neither of them exceeds the threshold
rule.mixed: exactly one of them exceeds the threshold

threshold_rationale: 0.10 lies at the geometric midpoint between the five-seed standard deviation of the baseline (0.055) and of the frozen configuration (0.190) on seeds 0-4 of the reported pass

result_sentences.method: Both did (standard deviations \AdvCfgSDThree{} and \AdvCfgSDSix), while the two configurations with near-zero adversarial weight stayed near the baseline's spread (\AdvCfgSDTwo{} and \AdvCfgSDFour), so the fragility belongs to the adversarial regime of the method and not only to the configuration we froze.
result_sentences.configuration: Neither did (standard deviations \AdvCfgSDThree{} and \AdvCfgSDSix), so the spread reported above belongs to the configuration selected at seed 0, and it was produced by the standard procedure of tuning once and training once.
result_sentences.mixed: Exactly one did (standard deviations \AdvCfgSDThree{} and \AdvCfgSDSix), so the experiment does not separate the two readings, and we report the attribution as unresolved.

selection_sentence: Tuning on each of the five seeds in turn would have selected the frozen configuration on \AdvCfgFrozenSelected{} of them.
caveat: t3 pairs a high adversarial weight with a high learning rate (2.06e-2), so its outcome alone cannot separate the two; t6 pairs a high weight with a low learning rate and is the cleaner test. t2 and t4 have near-zero weight and act as a within-method control.
